analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation edit to docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines 602-606, base line 602). It describes that model-weight verification reads uncached files through a reader thread that stays one 4 MiB chunk ahead of SHA-256 (WeightHasher.uncachedChunkBytes = 4 << 20, OverlappedFileDigest, two page-aligned buffers per hashed file), so disk reads and hashing run concurrently. The edit adds no code, environment variables, defaults, endpoints or trust-boundary changes. The surrounding text still says the full SHA is retained, the verified bytes and model arithmetic are unchanged, and the controls do not skip load checks or alter attestation policy. That is consistent with the threat model's weight-integrity assets and threats: A-004, T-012 and T-027.

I could not see the underlying Swift source for OverlappedFileDigest, so the following behaviors were not verified from the supplied evidence. A reviewer of the code change would need to check them: (1) the overlapped reader must hash exactly the bytes it reads, in order, and must not omit a short final chunk. (2) A read error on the background thread must fail the aggregate hash rather than yield a partial digest. (3) Concurrent hashing, with up to 4 workers and 2 buffers of 4 MiB per file, only adds a small bounded memory cost of about 8 MiB per file.

The documentation edit is not a security regression. The SSD prefix cache entries (T-041) and other configuration rows in the viewed ranges are unchanged. No new findings. Remaining integration question: the actual implementation in WeightHasher.swift is outside the supplied evidence and is the place where a hash-integrity regression could exist.
